items.heading: Explains that the Sefira of Keter comprises two phases: 1) the final phase of Ein Sof, for example, Malchut of Malchut of Ein Sof, called Atik. 2) It is the root of the emanated beings, and it is called Arich Anpin. The totality of both is called Keter. It contains four matters: — 1. There are no more than four phases in the ten Sefirot, HB TM, and Hochma is the first. 2. Keter is sometimes counted among the Sefirot and sometimes not counted among the Sefirot, and Daat is counted in its place. 3. Keter is an intermediary between the Emanator and the emanated being, and it contains two phases: 1) the phase of the Emanator, namely, for example, Malchut of Malchut of Ein Sof, called Tohu and Atik. 2) It is the phase of the emanated being, which is the root of the emanated beings, and is called Bohu or AA. 4. Similarly, Malchut of Malchut of the world of Atzilut is Atik in the world of Beria. — There are no more than four phases in any emanated being, HB TM, and Hochma is the first Sefira in the emanated being.
items.html: Now let us return to speaking of the upper worlds. After we have explained the allegory, let us now explain the object of the allegory, and let us say that 1the object of the allegory consists of only four elemental phases, which are the four letters of HaVaYaH, namely: Hochma, Bina, Tifferet, and Malchut, as above. Hence it follows that Hochma is called the first.

items.heading: Keter is sometimes counted among the ten Sefirot, and sometimes not counted, and Daat is counted in its place.
items.html: By this too you will understand what is said, that 2Keter is always an upper phase that is not included in that world; rather, it is like the crown of a king, which is above his head and is not part of his head. Hence it is not included in the Sefira, and Daat, mentioned in Sefer Yetzira, is counted in its place. Nevertheless, at times we do count it among the ten Sefirot. The matter will be understood by what was said above, that there is an intermediate phase between every phase and phase, similar to what the natural philosophers said, brought by the Ramban, of blessed memory, at the beginning of the verse, "And the earth was Tohu and Bohu." He also wrote, in the name of Sefer HaBahir, that before He created the four elements, He created one substance called Hyle, which is a thing prepared to receive the form of the four elements afterward, but it does not don any form at all. And what precedes the Tohu is called "nothing" (Efes), and it is regarded as coming from nothing and Tohu.

items.heading: Ein Sof is Efes (nothing), and after it comes Keter, called Tohu, and after it comes Bohu, which comprises the four elements.
items.html: The matter is that Ein Sof is called Efes, since there is no grasp of it whatsoever, 3for there is no substance there 4and no form at all. After it, 5Tohu came out, which is Keter, and after it, Bohu came out, comprising the four elements, HB TM.

items.heading: In Tohu there is the root of the four elements of the emanated being, in potential and not in actuality.
items.html: The explanation of the matter is that there must necessarily be an intermediate degree between the Emanator and the emanated being, since the distance between them is as the distance of the heavens from the earth; and how would one illuminate the other, and how would one create the other, being two extremes, unless there were something intermediate between them connecting them, being a phase close to the Emanator and close to the emanated being? Now, this phase is Keter, called 6Tohu, for it has no element at all, and is therefore not hinted at in the name HaVaYaH at all, only in the tip of the Yod; yet it is the intermediate phase, as above. This is because Keter is like the preceding substance called Hyle, which contains the root of all four elements, in potential and not in actuality, and is therefore called Tohu, because it makes (Tohe) the thoughts of men wonder, as they say, "Behold, we see that it has no form at all, 7yet we see that it is emanated, 8and it has the power of the four forms."

items.heading: With respect to Ein Sof, Keter may be called emanated; with respect to the emanated beings, it is the Emanator.
items.html: It follows that it may be called Ein Sof and Emanator, as is the opinion of some Kabbalists, that Ein Sof is Keter. And it may be called emanated, since Ein Sof is certainly greater than it, yet the sages warned about it, saying, "Do not inquire into what is beyond you." However, the utmost we can say about it is that Keter is the intermediate phase between Emanator and emanated being. The reason is that it is the final phase of all that is possible in Ein Sof, which 9emanated a single phase, in which is the root of all ten Sefirot, in concealment and great subtlety, such that no emanated being can be subtler than it. 10For above Tohu there is nothing else but the absolute nothing (Efes), as above.

items.heading: In Keter there are two phases: the final phase of Ein Sof, which emanated the second phase, which is the root of the emanated beings.
items.html: It follows that this phase has two degrees: the first is the lowest and most inferior of all the phase of Ein Sof, and it is as if we said, by way of illustration, that it is the phase of Malchut of Malchut, although it is not so, for there is no image or Sefira there whatsoever, God forbid; we speak this way only to soothe the ear. Now, this lowest degree of Ein Sof contains within it the totality of all that is above it, and receives from all of them, as is known, that Malchut receives from all. This lowest degree emanated the second phase, which is the highest degree of all that is in all the emanated beings, and in it is the root of all the emanated beings, and it bestows upon them all. Thus, the smallest of the Emanator emanated the most select of all the emanated beings, and there is no other degree at all between them, for after this Emanator, there is no emanated being closer to it and more similar to it than this.

items.heading: The phase of the Emanator in Keter is called Atik. And the phase of the root of the emanated beings in Keter is called Arich Anpin.
items.html: The totality of these two phases is a single phase called Keter. With respect to the first phase, some Kabbalists called it Ein Sof, and with respect to the second phase, some Kabbalists called it Keter, counted among the ten Sefirot. But our opinion is neither like the words of this one nor like the words of that one; rather, it is an intermediate phase between Ein Sof and the emanated beings, and it contains the phase of Ein Sof and the phase of the emanated beings. These two phases are called: Atik, and Arich Anpin. Both are called Keter, as is known to us, and understand this very well.

items.heading: The final phase in Atzilut, which is Malchut of Malchut of Atzilut, becomes Atik in the world of Beria, and clothes in the AA of Beria.
items.html: This is what is written elsewhere, that Malchut of Malchut of the world of Atzilut, which clothes in the head of Beria, which is Keter called Arich Anpin, is the phase of Atik of the world of Beria, and understand this very well.
